# Defensive Review

## System Overview
- AttackMap reviewed a web/service-facing codebase with 2 inferred entry points across 4 scanned files.
- Raw inferred entry points: 2
- Observed runtime/public surfaces: 2
- Protocol/lexicon-derived surfaces (inferred): 0
- Internal-only surfaces: 0
- Test/example/mocked surfaces (down-weighted): 0
- Languages: python
- Datastores: none
- External dependencies observed: 0
- Identified assets: 0 | controls observed: 0 | control absences: 2

## Notable Observations
- No notable cross-cutting observations were generated for this scan.

## ATT&CK Techniques Mapped
- `T1059` **Command and Scripting Interpreter** — _Execution_
- `T1078` **Valid Accounts** — _Privilege Escalation_
- `T1078.004` **Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts** — _Privilege Escalation_
- `T1190` **Exploit Public-Facing Application** — _Initial Access_
- `T1195` **Supply Chain Compromise** — _Initial Access_
- `T1195.001` **Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools** — _Initial Access_
- `T1528` **Steal Application Access Token** — _Credential Access_
- `T1552` **Unsecured Credentials** — _Credential Access_
- `T1552.001` **Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files** — _Credential Access_

## Detection Opportunities
- **Detection coverage for findings without a paired insight** _(signal=log)_
  - _Why:_ These findings did not generate cross-cutting insights but are still actionable with runtime telemetry.
  - _Suggested rule:_ Add per-finding logging at the affected handler with a structured `{finding_id, route, status_code}` payload, and aggregate in the SIEM.
  - _ATT&CK:_ `T1552`, `T1528`, `T1059`, `T1078`

## Asset Inventory
- No high-value assets identified from code signals.

## Defensive Controls

**Expected but not observed (control absences):**
- `csrf_protection` · CSRF protection — Public state-changing routes observed without CSRF markers.
- `rate_limiting` · Rate limiting — Public routes observed without any rate-limiting markers.

## Strengths
- Authentication/identity indicators are present in code signals (api_key).
- Secret usage appears environment-driven rather than hardcoded literals.
- 2 route(s) were classified as low-risk operational surfaces.

## Weaknesses / Risk Hotspots
- [HIGH | score 21.6] State-changing routes are reachable without an authentication control
- Reason: exposure=6.0, privilege=5.0, reachability=3.0
- Provenance: observed_runtime=100%, protocol_derived=0%, low_quality=0%
- [HIGH | score 20.1] Hard-coded secret literals were found in source or config
- Reason: exposure=6.0, confidence=4.5, reachability=3.0
- Provenance: observed_runtime=100%, protocol_derived=0%, low_quality=0%
- [MEDIUM | score 20.1] Secret-bearing environment variables are referenced in executable paths
- Reason: exposure=6.0, confidence=4.5, reachability=3.0
- Provenance: observed_runtime=100%, protocol_derived=0%, low_quality=0%
- Hotspot [score 15.0]: POST `/run` (`app.py:9`) -> public_api / low
- Reason: exposure=6.0, privilege=3.0
- Provenance: observed_runtime=100%, protocol_derived=0%, low_quality=0%

## Key Evidence Chains
- No explicit attack path was generated from current signals.

## Recommendations
- [observed] Require authentication (and server-side authorization) on every state-changing endpoint — attach an auth middleware/guard to the route or its router, a dependency/decorator on the handler, or a global policy that defaults to deny. Confirm the control actually runs before the handler mutates state.
- [observed] Rotate every detected credential immediately, purge it from git history, and move to environment-injected or vault-managed values. Anyone with read access to the repository already has these secrets.
- [observed] Confirm these secrets are injected securely, never logged or returned, rotated regularly, and scoped only to the privileges each route actually needs.
- [observed] Prefer argv-list subprocess calls with shell=False. Never interpolate request data into a shell string; validate and constrain any external command inputs.
- Add targeted tests for highest-risk routes and service edges to prevent regressions in boundary enforcement.

## Analyst Notes
- This defensive review is heuristic and intended as an engineering triage starting point.
- Validate top risks with repository-specific architecture context and runtime controls.
- Notable observations are cross-cutting hypotheses; treat them as triage prompts, not verdicts.

evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:11 [job 'build' step 'step'] — attacker-controlled ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} interpolated into run: script

weaknesses.title: OIDC token (id-token: write) available to pull-request-triggered workflow
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:3 [workflow (top-level permissions)] — id-token: *** on a pull_request_target-triggered workflow — PR code can mint cloud OIDC credentials

evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:8 [job 'build' step 'actions/checkout@v4'] — actions/checkout on pull_request_target without persist-credentials: false; later step job 'build' step 'step' runs code that can read the token from .git/config
findings.mitigation: `actions/checkout` persists the `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.git/config` by default. On `pull_request_target` / `issue_comment` / `workflow_run` jobs that later run PR code or artifacts, set `persist-credentials: false` so that code can't read the write-capable token.

findings.title: Unpinned GitHub Action (not pinned to a commit SHA)
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:8 [job 'build' step 'actions/checkout@v4'] — uses: actions/checkout@v4 (pin to a full commit SHA)
findings.mitigation: Pin third-party actions to a full 40-character commit SHA (`uses: org/action@<sha>`), not a moving tag or branch. A tag/branch lets the action owner — or anyone who compromises them — change what runs in your pipeline. Dependabot can keep the pinned SHAs updated.

evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:10 [job 'build' step 'actions/checkout@v4'] — pull_request_target checks out untrusted PR code: ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
findings.mitigation: `pull_request_target` runs with the base repo's secrets in scope. Don't check out and build the PR head ref in that context. Use `pull_request` for untrusted code, or check out only the base ref and never run fork-supplied build/test scripts with secrets available.

findings.title: Request-reachable OS command execution
findings.mitigation: Prefer argv-list subprocess calls with shell=False. Never interpolate request data into a shell string; validate and constrain any external command inputs.

findings.title: State-changing routes are reachable without an authentication control
evidence: POST /run in app.py:9 — no authentication/authorization control found on the route's chain
findings.mitigation: Require authentication (and server-side authorization) on every state-changing endpoint — attach an auth middleware/guard to the route or its router, a dependency/decorator on the handler, or a global policy that defaults to deny. Confirm the control actually runs before the handler mutates state.

findings.title: Secret-bearing environment variables are referenced in executable paths
findings.mitigation: Confirm these secrets are injected securely, never logged or returned, rotated regularly, and scoped only to the privileges each route actually needs.

findings.title: actions/checkout leaves the token in .git/config for untrusted code
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:8 [job 'build' step 'actions/checkout@v4'] — actions/checkout on pull_request_target without persist-credentials: false; later step job 'build' step 'step' runs code that can read the token from .git/config
findings.mitigation: `actions/checkout` persists the `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.git/config` by default. On `pull_request_target` / `issue_comment` / `workflow_run` jobs that later run PR code or artifacts, set `persist-credentials: false` so that code can't read the write-capable token.

findings.title: Debug mode or unrestricted management endpoints enabled
findings.mitigation: Never ship with debug mode on (Flask/Django `DEBUG`, Rails `consider_all_requests_local`) or Spring actuator endpoints exposed with `*`. Debug consoles leak internals and can enable RCE.

findings.title: Unpinned GitHub Action (not pinned to a commit SHA)
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:8 [job 'build' step 'actions/checkout@v4'] — uses: actions/checkout@v4 (pin to a full commit SHA)
findings.mitigation: Pin third-party actions to a full 40-character commit SHA (`uses: org/action@<sha>`), not a moving tag or branch. A tag/branch lets the action owner — or anyone who compromises them — change what runs in your pipeline. Dependabot can keep the pinned SHAs updated.

findings.title: CI script injection via untrusted context in a run: step
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:11 [job 'build' step 'step'] — attacker-controlled ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} interpolated into run: script

findings.title: Hard-coded secret literals were found in source or config

findings.title: OIDC token (id-token: write) available to pull-request-triggered workflow
